title: John, again
tomorrow: the council calls Peter and John ignorant men. why can't it stop them?

lines: I AM THE VINE: YOU THE BRANCHES.
cards: Houseplants have their own apps now: reminders to water, to turn the pot toward the light. But cut a stem off and no app can save it.
At the Last Supper in John's Gospel, Jesus says, in the Douay-Rheims Bible, "I am the vine: you the branches." A branch doesn't strain to make grapes. It has one job.

teach.h: ABIDE IN ME, AND I IN YOU.
teach.b: The word for that job is abide. "Abide in me, and I in you." It means stay, remain, make your home in.
John uses the same idea at the very start of his Gospel. Two people follow Jesus and ask where he's staying.
He says come and see, and they stay with him the rest of that day. The first thing anyone does with Jesus in John is not work. It's stay.

Now hold the week up to that vine. The night taught because John of the Cross stayed in the dark instead of leaving prayer. Merton's true self is found by staying still long enough to drop the costume.
Here I am is abiding said out loud. Out of Egypt was a walk toward a home with God. Justice and mercy is what grows on a branch that stays put.
And the father runs toward a son coming back to the vine.
One word under six carries: abide.

how: Catholics hear John 15 read at Mass in the Easter season; many pray before the tabernacle in quiet adoration, which they describe as staying, or abiding, with Christ.

o: the letter that warns of the end of time
the Gospel that opens with a family tree
the Gospel of the vine, the branches, and abide

games.q: the vine and the week — tap the pairs.
p: and they stayed with him that day

s: in John 15 a branch's job is to work hard at making fruit
its job is to stay on the vine; the fruit comes from abiding.
in John, the first two followers spend the day staying with Jesus
they ask where he's staying; he says come and see.
'abide' here means put up with something you dislike
it means stay, remain, make your home in.

games.q: your friend just started a new job in a new city, and she's burning out trying to keep up with everything at once. what does John 15 offer her?
o: stay connected to one root first; the rest grows from there.
cut every old connection so the new life can take hold.
work harder for now, since fruit depends on effort.
games.why: a branch bears fruit by staying on the vine, not by straining: abide in me, and I in you.

practice: Find one steady sound: a fan, traffic, your own breathing. Stay with it, the way a branch stays on the vine. When your mind wanders off, come back to the sound; that coming back is abiding.

wordCard.voice: John. The Gospel of the vine and the branches, and one plain word: abide.

orig.note: Greek, John 15:4: abide in me; remain, stay, make your home.

carryVoice: Hold on to this: abide, like a branch that simply stays on the vine. Week done, rest well.
